reviewer: Claude (claude-opus-5), independent narrow delta02 review continuing review01
subject: /tmp/opensip-implementation/m1-control-generation-subject-02
verdictScope: Narrow delta over the carriers and shape accepted in review01. It adds a conservative recursive ambiguous-union-property guard and a private-title collision refusal in prepare.py, plus 4 permanent test groups (82 total). All 8 output bodies and all 587 projections are unchanged. This is a finite guard for one identified alias class, not a universal Typify naming proof. It is not source promotion, exact source bridge, product integration, control/native/report semantics, or M1/product/release qualification.

correctionToReview01.statement: Review01's evidence text overstated the malformed-bound results.
correctionToReview01.detail: Review01 listed -1n, '0', 1.5, number 0, true, null, {} and [] as refused. My first work/ts/probe.cjs (like the author's check.cjs) omitted $schema, so those schemas were refused for 'unsupported schema dialect', not because of the bound. My later ts-direct-probe.json supplied the dialect and validly showed bound-specific refusal only for -1n and '0' ('nonnegative integer keyword required: x-maxUtf8Bytes') and for 1.5 and number 0 (EXACT_JSON_TYPE_REQUIRED). true, null, {} and [] were never validly tested in review01. The subject-02 permanent test covers -1n, true, '128', null, {} and [] with an explicit dialect and asserts that exact x-maxUtf8Bytes error. It passes here, and a mutation removing the keyword from the typed count set is caught.

advisories.title: Same-title / different-shape guard class has no permanent test
advisories.detail: Mutating the guard to allow the same title on different shapes survived all 4 new tests. My probe shows the real guard does refuse it, and it also refuses one-titled/one-untitled and empty-title cases. Add a permanent test for these.

advisories.title: Residual naming gaps outside the finite claim
advisories.detail: These pass without refusal: (a) a private title that differs from a definition name only by case or normalization; (b) a private title equal to a Typify-derived name for an untitled property elsewhere (definition RootVariant0 with property Property0 vs generated RootVariant0Property0); (c) differing allOf sibling properties; (d) branch properties nested inside a branch allOf. None occurs in the current 587 roots, which have independent roundtrip evidence from review01. If schemas widen, reserve normalized and derived names.

advisories.title: Runtime test resolves Node through PATH
advisories.detail: test_utf8_byte_bounds_on_runtime_template uses shutil.which('node'), not the closure-pinned node. It fails closed if node is missing, but it could run another Node or TypeScript host. It compiles runtime/*.ts templates, not the generated report.ts. That output is unchanged apart from headers and was covered in review01.

advisories.title: Invocation sensitivity should be documented exactly
advisories.detail: Without -I the execution tests refuse, as the root observed. With a non-pinned python3 on PATH, generation refuses ('tool executable differs from closure: python') and discovery errors. My own first run hit this because I set PATH to /usr/bin:/bin. I discarded it and reran with /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.14/bin/python3.14, whose hash matches the closure pin. Name the exact interpreter in the documented test command.

advisories.title: Review01 advisories status
advisories.detail: CA1 (bind the live source preflight and promote the exact raw schema through a reviewed unit), CA4 (the Rust carrier is inert and looser than the schema; control_protocol.rs is absent) and CA5 (stale openObligations; untracked route record) still apply. CA2 and CA3 are substantially addressed, apart from D2A1 and D2A2.

A post-review scan found no new __pycache__ in subject-01, subject-02, candidate-02 or validation-02. All imports and mutations ran on copies under work/ with -B and TMPDIR=work/tmp.

This matches root validation-02 source-preflight-refusal.json. The expected controlled refusal stands, and it is not promotion.
evidence.guardProbes: 39 probes. Refused: a differing array property under oneOf or anyOf at root, properties, items, additionalProperties, patternProperties, not, then, else, an allOf branch, and a nested-union branch (20); an untitled object under anyOf; an untitled object under a nested oneOf; differing const strings; the same title on different shapes; one titled and one untitled; an empty title; 2 identical + 1 different; namer title colliding with a definition; namer title colliding with an existing inline title. Passed as intended: differing plain strings, differing integer maxima, $ref children, distinct titles, and a direct definition-oneOf object (auto-titled). Informational gaps that pass: normalized-name collision, derived-name collision, allOf siblings, properties inside a branch allOf.
evidence.mutationSensitivity: Baseline: all 4 new tests pass. Caught by the target test: guard-noop, guard-not-called, guard-arrays-unneeded -> test_unhandled_union_property_aliases_refuse; reserved-check-removed -> test_variant_title_cannot_shadow_existing_owner; namer-disabled -> test_control_bodies_have_distinct_private_types; utf8-check-removed, utf8-scalar-count, utf8-off-by-one, bound-typecheck-removed -> test_utf8_byte_bounds_on_runtime_template. Survived: guard-same-title-allowed (D2A1).
evidence.invalidRunsDisclosed: My first test, mutation and generation attempts used /usr/bin python3 because I restricted PATH. They showed 44 tests with 9 errors, all-fail mutation baselines, and generation refused for a python closure mismatch. I discarded them as environment errors and reran everything with the pinned interpreter.

limits: The guard is a conservative check for one identified sibling-property alias class, not a proof over every Typify naming rule (see D2A2).
No Rust rebuild or roundtrip was rerun. Carrier bodies are byte-identical to subject-01, whose Rust roundtrip and swap evidence was accepted in review01, and the build04 closure is unchanged.
Adapter04 native confinement, sandbox and dependency algorithms were not re-audited, because this delta does not touch them.
Not reviewed: control/native/report semantics, exact source bridge, source promotion, native IDL, final report owner, product integration, and M1/product/release qualification.
The architecture and product checkouts were read only, and pins were checked by hash. The product repository has no commits, so no history-based custody was assessed.
